talks.title: Workplace Accommodation for Autisics
talks.summary:
### Neurodiversity and Sensory Architecture in the Workplace
At 00:00, Gerald R. Scott (Naval Postgraduate School) presents research on workplace accommodation and neurodiversity, focusing on sensory processing and environmental factors affecting autistic professionals in technology and cybersecurity fields.

### Designing Prosthetic Environments
At 07:03, Scott explores the concept of "prosthetic environments." He illustrates how physical office factors—such as open-floor plan acoustics, fluorescent lighting flicker, and irregular conversational interruptions—induce chronic sensory overload. Scott outlines physical adaptations, sound-dampening materials, and lighting modifications that mitigate environmental stressors.

### Cognitive Load, Executive Function, and Burnout
At 14:01, the presentation details findings from a qualitative study investigating executive function and task-switching friction. Scott explains that conventional corporate workflows often force autistic workers into prolonged masking, exhausting cognitive energy on social navigation rather than core technical problem-solving.

### Biometric Telemetry for Acute Stress Detection
At 21:02, Scott showcases biometric sensor validation. By tracking physiological metrics—including heart rate variability (HRV), galvanic skin response, and skin temperature—wearable sensors can identify early indicators of acute stress and cognitive overload before overt shutdowns occur.

### Talent Retention and Cognitive Diversity
Concluding at 28:00, Scott urges organizations to transition from deficit models to recognizing the strategic value of neurodiverse thinkers in technical roles. Implementing asynchronous communication, predictable schedules, and dedicated decompression zones allows enterprises to retain specialized talent while fostering healthier workplace cultures.

talks.title: DAY ONE
talks.summary:
### Kickoff and Scope of the Biohacking Village
At 00:00, Nina Alli and village organizers launch Day One of the DEF CON 26 Biohacking Village. The opening briefing introduces three core village tracks: medical device security evaluations in the Device Lab, biological defense and synthetic biology ethics, and healthcare cybersecurity policy.

### Medical Device Vulnerability Disclosure Realities
At 23:45, speakers discuss the ongoing state of coordinated vulnerability disclosure across healthcare manufacturing. They review common security flaws found in infusion pumps, telemetry servers, and pacemakers, stressing that finding bugs in medical hardware is standard engineering reality that requires transparent vendor collaboration.

### Biosecurity and Dual-Use Gene Editing Technologies
At 49:14, the presentation pivots to biological threats and synthetic biology. The speakers examine the democratization of CRISPR gene-editing tools, evaluating dual-use risks where accessible biotechnology could be misapplied toward pathogen engineering or agricultural bioterrorism.

### Translating Cyber Kill-Chain Doctrines to Healthcare
At 01:16:29, presenters adapt military and cyber defense doctrines to healthcare infrastructure. They demonstrate how twenty years of digital incident response, threat hunting, and defense-in-depth principles can be mapped onto medical operations to safeguard connected hospital environments.

### Genetic Privacy and Constitutional Protections
At 01:45:38, legal experts analyze the intersection of fourth amendment protections and commercial genomics. They address the privacy implications of law enforcement accessing direct-to-consumer genetic databases without warrants, calling for updated legal frameworks to safeguard biometric privacy.
